content: 1. A study conducted by Ospina-Tascón in 2021 compared high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) therapy to standard oxygen therapy for COVID-19 patients. The 28-day mortality rate was lower in the HFNC group (8 events out of 99 patients) compared to the standard oxygen therapy group (16 events out of 100 patients). The risk ratio (RR) was 0.51 (95% CI: 0.23–1.13), indicating a potential reduction in mortality with HFNC, though the confidence interval crossed 1, suggesting no statistically significant difference. 2. Perkins et al. in 2022 evaluated in-hospital mortality between HFNC and standard oxygen therapy. The HFNC group had 86 deaths among 405 patients, while the standard oxygen therapy group had 80 deaths among 359 patients. The risk ratio was 0.95 (95% CI: 0.73–1.25), showing no significant difference in mortality between the two groups. 3. For ICU mortality, Perkins (2022) reported 72 deaths in the HFNC group (251 patients) compared to 65 deaths in the standard oxygen therapy group (214 patients). The risk ratio was 0.94 (95% CI: 0.71–1.25), indicating no significant difference in ICU mortality. 4. Regarding intubation rates, Ospina-Tascón (2021) and Perkins (2022) found that HFNC was associated with a lower risk of intubation compared to standard oxygen therapy. The combined risk ratio was 0.84 (95% CI: 0.58–1.21), though heterogeneity was high (I² = 75%), and the overall effect was not statistically significant (P = 0.35). 5. ICU length of stay (LOS) was assessed in two studies. Ospina-Tascón (2021) reported a mean ICU LOS of 7 days (SD 5.93) for HFNC versus 9 days (SD 9.63) for standard oxygen therapy, with a mean difference of -2.00 days (95% CI: -4.22 to 0.22). Perkins (2022) reported a mean ICU LOS of 10.5 days (SD 15.6) for HFNC versus 9.6 days (SD 14.1) for standard oxygen therapy, with a mean difference of 0.90 days (95% CI: -1.20 to 3.00). The pooled mean difference was -0.53 days (95% CI: -3.37 to 2.31), with no significant difference between groups. 6. Hospital length of stay was also evaluated. Ospina-Tascón (2021) reported a mean hospital LOS of 12 days (SD 8.15) for HFNC versus 14 days (SD 10.37) for standard oxygen therapy, with a mean difference of -2.00 days (95% CI: -4.59 to 0.59). Perkins (2022) reported a mean hospital LOS of 18.3 days (SD 20) for HFNC versus 17.1 days (SD 18) for standard oxygen therapy, with a mean difference of 1.20 days (95% CI: -1.49 to 3.89). The pooled mean difference was -0.42 days (95% CI: -3.56 to 2.71), showing no significant difference. 7. In non-randomized controlled trials (n-RCTs), HFNC was compared to standard oxygen therapy for overall mortality. Seven studies, including Kabak (2021), Aguirre-Bermeo (2021), and Beduneau (2021), reported a pooled risk ratio of 0.89 (95% CI: 0.69–1.14), with moderate heterogeneity (I² = 60%). This suggests no significant difference in overall mortality between HFNC and standard oxygen therapy. 8. ICU mortality in n-RCTs was assessed in four studies, including Aguirre-Bermeo (2021) and Wendel-Garcia (2022). The pooled risk ratio was 1.14 (95% CI: 0.91–1.44), with moderate heterogeneity (I² = 41%), indicating no significant difference in ICU mortality. 9. Hospital mortality in n-RCTs was reported by Beduneau (2021), with a risk ratio of 1.26 (95% CI: 1.00–1.57), suggesting a potential increase in hospital mortality with HFNC, though the confidence interval included 1. 10. For 30-day mortality, Beduneau (2021), Bonnet (2021), and Hansen (2021) reported a pooled risk ratio of 0.74 (95% CI: 0.38–1.46), with high heterogeneity (I² = 81%), indicating no significant difference between HFNC and standard oxygen therapy. 11. Intubation rates in n-RCTs were assessed in six studies, including Sayan (2021) and Wendel-Garcia (2022). The pooled risk ratio was 0.77 (95% CI: 0.72–0.81), indicating a statistically significant reduction in intubation rates with HFNC. 12. In randomized controlled trials (RCTs), HFNC was compared to non-invasive ventilation (NIV), continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP), or other non-HFNC modalities. RamachandranNair (2021) reported a risk ratio of 0.63 (95% CI: 0.38–1.04) for overall mortality, favoring HFNC but not reaching statistical significance. 13. Intubation rates in RCTs comparing HFNC to NIV/CPAP were reported by RamachandranNair (2021), with a risk ratio of 0.59 (95% CI: 0.35–0.99), indicating a statistically significant reduction in intubation rates with HFNC. 14. Hospital length of stay in RCTs was evaluated by RamachandranNair (2021) and Perkins (2022). The pooled mean difference was 0.66 days (95% CI: -1.11 to 2.43), showing no significant difference between HFNC and NIV/CPAP. 15. In n-RCTs comparing HFNC to NIV/CPAP, overall mortality was assessed in seven studies, including Franco (2020) and Santos (2022). The pooled risk ratio was 0.63 (95% CI: 0.48–0.82), indicating a statistically significant reduction in mortality with HFNC. 16. ICU mortality in n-RCTs was reported by Beduneau (2021) and Wendel-Garcia (2022), with a pooled risk ratio of 0.64 (95% CI: 0.53–0.77), favoring HFNC. 17. Hospital mortality in n-RCTs was assessed in two studies, with a pooled risk ratio of 0.50 (95% CI: 0.41–0.61), indicating a significant reduction in hospital mortality with HFNC. 18. For 30-day mortality, Franco (2020) and Beduneau (2021) reported a pooled risk ratio of 0.53 (95% CI: 0.43–0.67), favoring HFNC. 19. Intubation rates in n-RCTs were assessed in eight studies, including Franco (2020) and Santos (2022). The pooled risk ratio was 0.90 (95% CI: 0.78–1.04), showing no significant difference between HFNC and NIV/CPAP. 20. ICU length of stay in n-RCTs was evaluated by Beduneau (2021) and Costa (2022). The pooled mean difference was -0.94 days (95% CI: -4.17 to 2.28), showing no significant difference. 21. Hospital length of stay in n-RCTs was assessed in six studies, including Franco (2020) and Wendel-Garcia (2022). The pooled mean difference was 0.83 days (95% CI: -1.10 to 2.76), showing no significant difference. 22. For 30-day or in-hospital mortality, Franco (2020) and Santos (2022) reported a pooled risk ratio of 0.51 (95% CI: 0.43–0.61), favoring HFNC. 23. In RCTs comparing HFNC to invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), Aguirre-Bermeo (2021) reported a risk ratio of 0.78 (95% CI: 0.45–1.36) for ICU mortality, showing no significant difference. 24. Intubation rates in RCTs comparing HFNC to IMV were reported by Aguirre-Bermeo (2021), with a risk ratio of 0.52 (95% CI: 0.42–0.64), indicating a significant reduction in intubation rates with HFNC. 25. ICU length of stay in RCTs comparing HFNC to IMV was reported by Aguirre-Bermeo (2021), with a mean difference of -2.00 days (95% CI: -5.61 to 1.61), showing no significant difference.
